question: What is another common name for a lumbar puncture?
explanation: A lumbar puncture is commonly referred to as a spinal tap because it involves accessing fluid from the spinal column. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which main body fluid is collected during a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Spot on! The procedure draws cerebrospinal fluid from around the spinal cord to help doctors run diagnostic tests. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which of these is a major reason why a doctor would order a lumbar puncture?
explanation: You got it! Testing cerebrospinal fluid is key to diagnosing central nervous system infections like meningitis. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why is a lumbar puncture very dangerous for a patient with a brain mass causing high pressure inside the skull?

options.A: It will stop the heart instantly

explanation: Exactly. Releasing fluid when pressure is already high can push brain tissue downward. Safety first—always check for high intracranial pressure! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h2)

question: In an adult, around which part of the spine does the main spinal cord usually end?
explanation: Well done! The cord ends near L1, which is why doctors insert the needle lower down where it's safer. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which body landmark helps a clinician easily find the L4 spot for a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Correct! Drawing an imaginary line across the top of the hip bones (iliac crests) points right to the L4 space. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which drug history is most important for a nurse to check before a patient has a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Spot on! Blood thinners (anticoagulants) raise the risk of dangerous bleeding around the spine. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h4)

question: Your patient is heading for a lumbar puncture in 30 minutes. What is a helpful nursing action right now?
explanation: Great job! An empty bladder keeps the patient comfortable while they curl up on their side for the procedure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the best position for a patient during a standard lumbar puncture?

options.A: Sitting straight upright with arms down
options.D: Flat on the back with legs straight

explanation: You nailed it! Curling up on the side like a fetus opens up the spaces between the back bones. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why does the nurse gently help the patient tuck their chin and knees tight together during this procedure?

options.A: To keep the back muscles completely relaxed
options.B: To open up the spaces between the vertebrae
options.C: To slow down the heart rate during the tap
options.D: To prevent the patient from biting their tongue

explanation: Exactly! Flexing the spine widens the gaps, making it much easier for the doctor to insert the needle safely. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h5)

question: How is a patient usually positioned immediately after a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Spot on! Lying flat helps the tiny puncture hole seal up and lowers the chance of a stubborn spinal headache. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why should the nurse encourage the patient to drink plenty of fluids after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To flush out remaining local anesthetic drugs
options.B: To prevent high blood pressure spikes
options.C: To keep the patient awake and alert
options.D: To help replace the lost cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: You got it! Fluids help the body quickly make up for the cerebrospinal fluid that was removed. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h6)

question: What should healthy, normal cerebrospinal fluid look like?
explanation: Correct! Normal cerebrospinal fluid looks just like clean, pure water. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h7)

question: What does cloudy cerebrospinal fluid usually tell the medical team?

options.A: Presence of excess oxygen in the brain
options.B: High levels of dietary sugar in the blood
options.C: Presence of white blood cells from infection
options.D: Normal aging process of the nervous system

explanation: Well done! Cloudiness usually means white blood cells are crowded in there fighting off an infection like meningitis. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the most common side effect or complication after a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Spot on! A post-dural puncture headache happens quite often when a little fluid continues to leak out. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h8)

question: How can you tell if a patient has a typical post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It only hurts when the patient eats or drinks
options.B: It disappears completely when the room is dark
options.C: It gets worse when the patient sits or stands up
options.D: It stays the exact same intensity all day long

explanation: You nailed it! These headaches get worse when upright because of lower fluid pressure around the brain, and they feel better when lying flat. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h8)
